experiment: E6: gene-gene dependence on real data at a fixed mean
question: On real data, do dispersion choices that change calibration also change how well decoded cells reproduce gene-gene correlations?
fits: the saved E2 PCA-512 negative-binomial decoders (Arm A and Arm B, fit seeds 42-44); fitted means and per-cell dispersions on validation and test cells
draws: Poisson, shared per-gene (median validation dispersion) and per-cell, all at the same fitted mean; the E1 draw seeds
groups: dataset x cell-type groups with at least 20 test and 20 validation cells
genes: within each group, the 30 decoded genes with the highest mean count among the group's training cells
endpoint: correlation error: median absolute difference between off-diagonal Pearson correlations of log1p expression in decoded and real test cells; pairs with an undefined correlation in either matrix are skipped
reference: the same error between the group's real validation and real test cells (an independent real sample)
secondary: expressed-gene calibration error of each draw on the same group
inference_stats: seeds averaged within group, groups within dataset; equal-weight mean over datasets; 2000-resample dataset-cluster bootstrap (seed 20261110); share of groups in which calibration improves while correlation error increases
retention: all groups, seeds and arms retained
